e: DC takes a familiar oppression-and-police-brutality setup and packages it as a surprisingly effective commercial entertainer. The performances, cinematography and especially the classical-music-infused BGM made the violence land far better for me than I expected.
v: A brutal oppression drama wrapped in proper commercial packaging — and for audiences like me, that packaging is exactly what makes it click 😄
body:
I generally stay away from the overcooked Tamil-flavoured oppression & brutality stories... but couldn’t control myself with all the FOMO created by the feedback from those who watched it. So much so that I had to ditch Srinu, my regular Partner in Crime for watching such movies!!!! 😜

And do I have any regret or guilt about ditching him? Absolutely not 😉 But can’t deny the fact that I would have enjoyed it even more in his company!!! Don’t worry Srinu, we will compensate with Toxicity 😉😂

Coming back to the movie... unlike the epics of Kabali or Kaala, DC is a proper oppression and fight-against-police-brutality movie, but packed into a proper commercial entertainer that somehow still feels realistic. And that’s largely because of the extraordinary effort from all the actors, cinematographer and music director 🙏

Special mention to the BGM 🤯 I feel Animal started the trend of using old songs to elevate the audience experience of a scene, which Dhurandhar bettered by using vintage & contrasting songs as BGM for violent scenes. But DC took it one step further by using classical music to elevate the emotions during violence 🫡 What a combination!!!

Initially, I was surprised to hear that this movie wasn’t doing that well with the Tamil audience but clicked really well with the Telugu audience. After watching it, I understood why.

Tamil movie lovers still cherish those raw, grounded and realistic oppression movies, whereas this one is packaged commercially. That may not have worked as much for them... but for audiences like me, that commercial packaging is exactly what made it click 😄

e: The scale, locations, CGI and performances are unquestionably richer this time, but the magic that made Kantara work for me is missing. I kept seeing a commercially upgraded spectacle when I was hoping for a deeper dive into the folklore and origins behind the legend.
v: A visual spectacle with terrific performances, but for me it remains exactly this: Too Much Quality with No Clarity.
body:
DISCLAIMER: Don’t worry, I’m not on some secret mission to hate or hype this movie. This is just what I honestly felt after watching it — NO FAN CLUB, NO HATE CLUB. Just me and my opinion.

When I first watched Kantara, I didn’t have any expectations and I was completely blown away by the approach of blending folklore, terrific visuals and acting into a very simple and common story of a land dispute.

Coming to Kantara: Chapter 1, obviously I had expectations from the previous movie...

On the positive side... this time the budget has been hiked, and you can see the grandeur on the big screen with the story being set in a king’s era. The locations looked more realistic than in the previous part. The CGI work was more polished, the cast had more familiar faces this time, and everyone did an excellent job.

For Kantara, I remember how I was going bonkers about how Rishab Shetty had written, directed and acted in the movie... This time too, he did it all by himself. Unfortunately, what worked for me in Kantara didn’t work for me in Kantara: Chapter 1.

My eyes were in for a treat with the visual spectacle on screen, but somehow it wasn’t creating the much-needed impact on my other senses 😪 All I could think of was a commercially upgraded version made to cash in on the craze of Kantara.

The BGM again felt like a rehashed version of Kantara and failed to create much impact for me this time. Acting-wise, Rishab Shetty was good as usual, but this time I always knew how his hand and leg movements would be and how his facial expressions would change whenever he was possessed. It felt like I was watching the same Kantara performance again, so the Vaaaaaaaaav feeling was missing this time.

Special shout-out to Gulshan Devaiah, who was excellent as King Kulashekara and was the only reason I didn’t think of walking out of this film with disappointment 🫡

Also, if not for the individual performances by Rukmini and Jayaram, there was hardly any scope in the story — except in the climax — to elevate their characters, because the movie was only and only focused on elevating Rishab.

When the film itself is named Chapter 1, I was expecting Rishab Shetty to dive deep into his region’s folklore and give us the origin story of Panjurli, Guliga, Bhoota Kola and finally how Kantara was formed... but instead, he focused on exploring the story of tribal leader Berme, played by Rishab himself.

While Kantara’s execution revolved around the land dispute and how Guliga protects Panjurli’s land and promise, with Rishab Shetty’s character moulding itself perfectly into the story flow, Chapter 1 is all about the commercial rise, fall and rise of Berme — with the actual story going for a toss!!!!

On a final note... Kantara: Chapter 1 is Too Much Quality with No Clarity.

e: The story is below average and neutral viewers may not get the same high, but Sujeeth knows exactly what kind of film he is making. A handful of adrenaline-pumping PK moments, powered by Thaman’s terrific BGM, are enough to turn OG into a proper fan celebration.
v: Average gangster content on paper, but Sujeeth + Thaman turn it into a proper PK fan trance — and the forgotten fan in me was fully satisfied!
body:
It’s truly a Pawan Kalyan film — made for the fans, by the fans, and dedicated to the fans!

The bigger the fan, the stronger the trance this movie creates. Fans will definitely watch it multiple times just to relive the high.

For neutral audiences, the movie might feel like average commercial content, similar to films like Jailer, Leo, Pathaan or Good Bad Ugly.

Content-wise, it follows the regular commercial gangster format, with stylish scenes and terrific background music from Thaman 🙏 The story itself is below average and can test your patience. The much-hyped Saaho connection also didn’t fit in well for me.

Still, I admire Sujeeth’s effort. He had to work with very limited dates from Pawan, who has always relied more on his screen charisma than acting range. Within those limits, Sujeeth managed to create 4–5 adrenaline-pumping scenes that drove fans crazy and made them forget the flaws.

Thaman’s music elevated the film into a treat for fans. He is the real HERO of this movie — I can’t even dare to imagine this film without his BGM 🙏🙏

Neutral viewers may not enjoy it as much as fans. My real frustration, however, is with self-proclaimed reviewers who criticise every movie without understanding its intent. This film was always promoted as a cult fan movie, not a national-award-level story. Expecting otherwise is just unfair and shows just how big an IDIOT you are.

Though I usually watch films as a neutral movie lover, Sujeeth succeeded in waking up the long-forgotten PK fan in me — and satisfied him to the core!

e: MIRAI gets a lot right with its mythology-meets-commercial-cinema idea, impressive CGI, production values and committed performances. But the hero, villain and Ashoka’s hidden-books mythology deserved far more depth; what could have been an epic multipart franchise feels rushed into one film.
v: A VERY GOOD mythological superhero entertainer with spectacular CGI — but as a film buff, I can’t stop seeing the EPIC franchise opportunity that was missed 😢
body:
Let me make this clear: this is not a Cult Classic Movie, but it is a VERY GOOD movie with a proper mix of fiction & mythology along with commercial elements!!! A good movie about how an underdog turns into a superhero with a touch of the Puranas!!!

Wait a minute... why do I have a déjà vu of reviewing Hanu-Man!! Teja Sajja should have done at least a movie or two before committing to MIRAI, just to give the audience a fair chance to enjoy this movie without constantly comparing it with Hanu-Man!!!

Content-wise, the film had a lot to explore in the villain’s arc, the hero’s arc and their final clash — enough potential to become a multipart movie with a grand climax. But somewhere, I felt the director rushed into making the entire story a single-part movie.

When normal commercial movies like Devara and Kingdom have forcefully dragged their stories to make them two-part films, I am totally disappointed in Karthik, who is the writer and director here, for not putting a little more effort into the depth of the content. There was so much scope to make the story more informative about Ashoka’s nine hidden books and their contents, and to establish both the villain and hero’s character arcs properly. Instead, the film rushes to finish everything in a single part, leaving a few loose ends and a sense of dissatisfaction.

The execution of the CGI is the saving grace of this movie, along with top-notch production values. There are a few scenes that genuinely give you the vibe of watching a high-budget movie, and the team deserves special appreciation for that.

The BGM was very good and highlights the CGI-heavy scenes to give goosebumps for sure.

Acting-wise, Teja Sajja was perfect as an underdog-turned-superhero, but as I mentioned, he already played a similar character in Hanu-Man — the main difference being a village boy there versus a street-smart city boy here.

Manchu Manoj was perfect for this role and did complete justice to it. I only feel bad for him because the story writers didn’t put in that extra effort to dive deeper into his character. With stronger character-building, this could have become one of the most memorable villain roles in Indian movies — something on the level of Thanos.

Shriya Saran as Ambika was refreshing casting and she did complete justice to her role. Except for the Hindi Drishyam films, where she played a more conventional housewife character, I don’t think she has had many author-backed roles to properly showcase her acting skills — and man, she impressed me a lot here 😍

On a final note... this movie had everything in it to become an EPIC Multipart Franchise, potentially even bigger in scope than Baahubali or KGF, only to be let down by some lazy effort in the story-writing and screenplay departments 😡

As a normal audience member, you may either like this movie to the core or simply feel it is a good one-time watch. But as a film buff, I could easily see a Golden Opportunity Missed 😢

e: Little Hearts avoids both the loud youth-film template and the overly poetic love-story route. Its simple writing, likeable performances and honest climax made it a nostalgic, light-hearted watch that may not demand a big screen, but absolutely deserves your time.
v: A simple, wholesome and genuinely feel-good teenage love story that stays light, realistic and family-friendly — exactly where its charm lies ❤️
body:
A wholesome family entertainer that captures teenage love in a fun, light-hearted way. It’s sure to take you on a nostalgic trip back to your carefree college days, filled with laughter and feel-good moments!!!!

Kudos to director-writer Sai Marthand for presenting the story so realistically that you feel connected to almost every scene. As the movie went on, I kept wondering how he would handle the climax — would he take the typical cinematic route of convincing the parents, or go completely offbeat? And if he did, would that still fit the film’s realistic, feel-good tone?

Hats off to him for delivering the climax in such a simple and honest way. It may feel a little abrupt for regular moviegoers, but that’s exactly how life works 🙏

The lead pair of Mouli and Shivani Nagaram looked cute on screen and did a fantastic job. And it’s not only them — the whole friends gang, along with seasoned performers Rajeev, Anitha, Kanchi and Satya, did full justice to their roles.

Usually, teenage love stories are shown in two ways: one like Boys or Bus Stop, filled with bold scenes and cuss words to attract the youth; and the other like Bommarillu or Kotha Bangaru Lokam, which are more poetic and cinematic, aiming to become timeless classics.

Here, the director chooses a different path — keeping it light-hearted and family-friendly while still getting his message across. And that’s exactly where I got totally impressed.

Having said that, not everyone may feel this needs to be watched on the big screen. It doesn’t offer a grand cinematic experience, extraordinary content or a huge star cast that makes a theatrical watch mandatory. But you still won’t regret watching it in a theatre because it gives you some wonderful light-hearted moments.

If you don’t want to watch it on the big screen, then please don’t miss it on OTT. This could easily have become the talk of the town after streaming, but kudos to the team — especially whoever handled the promotions — for releasing it among bigger films and still creating enough buzz to pull audiences into theatres.

And believe me... you won’t regret watching it on the big screen either 😊

e: COOLIE worked better for me once I stopped expecting another LCU event or a conventional Rajinikanth vehicle. Soubin Shahir is the real acting star, Anirudh powers nearly every elevation, but the final 30 minutes and some wasted cameos drag down an otherwise enjoyable film.
v: I liked most of COOLIE — especially Soubin, Nagarjuna’s swag and Anirudh’s BGM — but that horrible final stretch needs a VERY BIG forgiving heart 😉
body:
I liked this movie, barring the last 30 minutes... I think the over-expectations on Loki as a director, and all the anticipation of this being blended into the LCU, contributed a lot to the disappointing reactions.

Also, to be fair... this is not a typical Rajinikanth movie where he takes centre stage throughout. To be frank, this is Soubin Shahir’s movie, with Rajini playing a highly impactful extended lead presence 😉

Man, what a performer Soubin is 🫡 With his acting ability, he simply outshines all the so-called commercial stars around him. If you actually watch the movie from the perspective of Soubin being the key character, you may enjoy it a lot more.

Nagarjuna was good in parts. He looked stunning in that dapper, ultra-kool villain look and totally owned a few scenes with his swag!!! But unfortunately, apart from being stylish, he doesn’t have much of a character to play. And in the climax, where he is supposed to deliver a few intimidating lines, the dialogue delivery didn’t work for me at all.

Credit to my friend Srinivas for coming up with this gem: “Nagarjuna voice lo evadinanna bhayapettali ani warning isthunte, vinevadiki mathram ento veedu bhayapaduthu maatladuthunnattu untundi.” 😂

Aamir Khan’s character was a total waste and wasn’t even necessary. Just to fit him into the movie, the climax gets dragged by another 15 minutes 🫩 And did he make an impact? NO. For me, he looked completely buffoonish. The inevitable comparison with Rolex from Vikram only makes the scene feel worse 🤢

Rajinikanth was at his general best, and maybe after decades he tried playing someone who isn’t all-powerful — someone who can make mistakes — and he fits into that space nicely.

Shruti Haasan was okayish. And I won’t talk too much about Upendra’s presence because I feel Loki completely failed to utilise Uppi’s talent. Still waiting for some director — apart from Upendra himself — who can unleash the actor within him 🫩

Anirudh is the only true star of this movie for me. His BGM elevates almost every character and every major moment. I honestly can’t imagine watching this film without that background score 🫡

Overall, you may like COOLIE if you can be saint enough — like me 😇 — to leave behind all expectations from Loki’s previous films, forget the huge star cast, and have a BIG SUITABLE HEART to forgive the horrible last 30 minutes 😉

e: WAR2 delivers the familiar YRF spy template without surprising me much. NTR deserves credit for taking on a role opposite Hrithik, but the writing wastes his emotional strengths and turns the clash into another body-flexing exercise where Hrithik naturally owns the screen.
v: Exactly the kind of YRF spy movie I expected — not disappointing, not particularly great either... but Hrithik’s charisma still makes a strong case for him as the next James Bond 🙏
body:
Knowing the history of the YRF Spy Franchise, I knew exactly what to expect from this kind of movie. And I can say I was NOT DISAPPOINTED — though I also never had the feeling that I had watched a very good movie.

No matter how it was promoted in Telugu, we always knew that Hrithik aka Kabir is the hero of the WAR franchise, and any other actor — no matter how big or small — would eventually be sidelined as the story progresses. That’s exactly what happened in WAR2 as well, and I have no complaints.

In fact, I got a chance to see NTR as an artist rather than only as a hero. Am I totally impressed with how that opportunity was used? That’s debatable...

If we look at YRF spy-verse movies like Pathaan and Tiger 3, we have seen SRK and Salman do cameos in each other’s films while conveniently avoiding either bringing Hrithik into their movies or appearing in his. And I can understand why — with his Greek-God looks and swag, Hrithik can simply steal the limelight 😄

That’s exactly why I’m impressed with NTR for taking up the challenge of being cast opposite Hrithik. Unfortunately, he was let down by a poor character arc. The director failed to use NTR’s emotional acting power to balance Hrithik’s charisma and instead chose the same old template of body-flexing between the two — a battle Hrithik clearly dominates effortlessly.

That may be a problem for hardcore fans who insist on seeing NTR only as a HERO. But they need to accept that he is effectively the antagonist here. Once you accept that, you can enjoy the movie just like any other spy film.

I actually wanted to watch the Hindi version, but ended up watching it in Telugu after Chimtu (Naga Vamsi) anna’s speech — he practically blackmailed TFI yuvatha into pushing the Telugu numbers above Hindi 😂

That turned out to be another mistake. I strongly felt the Hindi version would have given me a better experience because the Telugu dubbing was surprisingly poor, especially considering NTR himself is part of the film ☹️

YRF should seriously give the spy movies a proper gap and start looking for fresh ideas. Their recent spy films keep following the same repeated pattern — focus on Hero vs Villain combinations, sprinkle in guest appearances, repeat.

And finally... I strictly believe Hrithik should be the next James Bond. I would like to officially start a petition for that 🙏

e: Hari Hara Veera Mallu was a painful theatrical experience for me: a fundamentally awkward story, visibly poor VFX, years of production baggage and a trailer that appears to have contained nearly all the best material. My wife tried to stop this review... but even hunger couldn’t save it 😢😂
v: A movie that survived every warning from nature only to become my new No. 1 khalakhandam — even KANNAPA and ADIPURUSH deserve my apology 🙏😂
body:
Though I watched this First Day First Show, I was forced not to share my experience by none other than my wife — who is a HARDCORE POWER STAR FAN — under threat of dire consequences at home 😢

Fearing the possibility of not getting food, I held back my post... only to realise: “Hum khaana nahi brathak saktha, but review post pettakunda nahi brathak saktha hum!!!” 😂

To start with, I would like to sincerely apologise to Manchu Vishnu anna and Om Raut for trolling them for their respective khalakhandas KANNAPA & ADIPURUSH... this movie beats both of them to take my No. 1 spot 🙏

Some movies are simply never meant to be made, and even nature tries to warn you — pandemics, director changes, financial issues, the hero becoming busy with an entirely different career path...

But if the producer is still adamant about investing, completing and releasing the movie, then he is not a human being with a normal gunde. Definitely GUNDE LO GUNNAPAM diginodu maatrame cheyagaladu!!! Just to reiterate, I said GUNDE... and I really mean it. Meeru vere arthalu teesukovaddu 🙏😂

Story-wise, how exactly do you give a heroic ending to a commercial film when you select Aurangzeb as your villain? You obviously can’t show your hero killing him. And then you also want the hero to steal the Koh-i-Noor?

I have a feeling Krish understood this basic story problem after shooting some portions and quietly left the project 😅 The project probably should have been shelved right there, but I have no idea who remained so adamant about completing it.

Then came the Eureka moment. In the last few months, ChatGPT and Grok started generating basic images and videos from prompts... so maybe the makers used the trial versions 🙏 Because the graphics genuinely look like the quality you get from free AI tools.

And to address the story problem, the remaining portions seem to have been reshaped into a very weak adaptation of Pawan’s Sanathana political stance.

When they said Jyothi Krishna was the second director who completed the pending portions... did they actually mean he was the one typing the PROMPTS into ChatGPT to generate those graphics? 🫡

It was literally painful to the eyes — again, I said 👀 — to watch such poor-quality VFX on a quality INOX screen 🫩

Everyone already had very low expectations for this movie. Forget the result — at one point we weren’t even sure whether it would release 🤷 Then the trailer made me feel that maybe it wouldn’t be as bad as I feared.

Sadly, after watching the film, I realised the trailer had almost all the best scenes of the entire movie... and THAT’S IT!!!!

In a way, I guess this movie is Pawan Kalyan’s sweet revenge on his fans for constantly complaining that he wasn’t doing straight films. After this, nobody will dare complain again 😂

FINGERS CROSSED FOR OG!!!! 🙏

e: THAMMUDU has the bones of a commercial emotional drama, but the painfully linear narration drains the masala, tension and emotion out of it. The cinematography is excellent and Laya’s comeback is welcome, but the writing left Srinu and me wondering why we ignored all warning signs.
v: An emotional movie with the unique ability to make you feel absolutely NO emotion — Srinu and I almost needed a psychiatrist after this one 🙏😪
body:
Before going into my experience of the movie, let me introduce Srinu — my Partner in Crime for watching movies. Together, we have witnessed many epics and disasters over the past 15-odd years 🙏

While we were stepping into AMB to watch this movie, Srinu asked me: “Poorna, did you realise this is the first time we are watching a Nithiin movie on the First Day? Can you please explain why we are doing this?”

My answer was simple: “I don’t know, Srinu.” Even the trailer looked pretty ordinary to me, but I had seen a few so-called honest interviews and interactions between Dil Raju and Nithiin that raised my curiosity. And then there was the fact that the movie got an A certificate, which they claimed was justified by the content. Somehow, all of this tempted me into watching it on Day 1 itself!!!!

After the movie, while walking out of AMB, I asked Srinu another question: “Srinu, naakante siggu ledhu — prathi movie ki edo oka reason cheppi tempt avutha... neekaina buddhi undakkarla? ‘Vaddu Poorna’ ani cheppachu ga!!!!”

And as usual, Srinu never answers or reacts. He simply tried to cover up his pain with a smile 🙏

Srinu and I seriously considered searching for a psychiatrist nearby to check whether we had both lost sensitivity in our hearts. We had just watched a film packed with supposedly emotional scenes, yet neither of us felt even a little emotion.

Then we realised it wasn’t us. It is the unique ability of director Sreeram Venu to direct an Emotional Movie Without Emotions 😪

We have seen plenty of so-called Hollywood & OTT movie watchers — self-proclaimed intellectuals 😜 — complain that Tollywood kills interesting stories by commercialising them with unnecessary comedy, elevations and masala.

They especially criticised Sreeram Venu for turning MCA with Nani into an out-and-out commercial movie. THAMMUDU is the perfect slipper-shot answer to them. After sitting through this very linear and non-engaging storytelling, even they may start begging the director to add some masala 😂

Fun fact: the basic setup reminded me so much of MCA, except this time almost all the commercial formula has been removed. A proper tribute to MCA indeed! And the irony is that Nani was reportedly supposed to play this character but somehow escaped 😳

Story-wise, the movie had enough scope to become a proper mass-commercial entertainer. For some unknown reason, the director chose to narrate it in a completely non-commercial format 🙄 And please don’t assume he is an offbeat filmmaker — this is the same man who directed MCA 😂

The very thought of taking a potentially commercial story and presenting it in such a non-commercial way should fetch the whole team an Oscar 🫡

The confusion is visible even in basic relationships. The film never clearly establishes whether Varsha is Nithiin’s love interest or simply a good friend. It almost feels like the director thought calling her a heroine would be too “routine commercial”, tried to make the relationship sound offbeat, and finally landed on the word COMPANION — which I am still trying to decode 🤔

I genuinely feel bad for Nithiin. Many of his recent movies appear to have hit potential on paper but have been mishandled in execution. Robinhood drowned itself in commercial elements; THAMMUDU has almost none. Hope he finds the right balance between content and commercial cinema soon.

Saurabh Sachdeva is also being overused by Tollywood directors. His mannerisms and expressions felt unique in Animal, but when every film gives him unusual behaviour without properly using it later, the same style starts feeling loud and over-the-top.

I personally felt Laya was overrated during her original run and that being a Telugu heroine helped her image. She chose her roles intelligently, but I honestly don’t remember audiences desperately missing her when she stepped away from films. Yet, for a change, her comeback is one of the few genuinely interesting things in this movie 🙏

The cinematography is top-notch and blends beautifully with the forest locations. Which brings me to my biggest question: why did Manchu anna choose New-Zealand-resort-type forests for KANNAPA instead of these beautiful rustic locations? 🤔🤔

And finally, while I was wondering why this film received an A certificate, my friend — Living Legend Srinu — enlightened me: maybe the censor board simply wanted to save as many lives as possible from the depression of watching an emotional movie and discovering that you still couldn’t feel anything 🙏😂

e: KANNAPA’s core devotional material could have worked as a short, focused film, but the bloated runtime, weak VFX, strange diction, over-the-top presentation and unintentionally funny first half made it a torturous experience for me. Prabhas is the rare relief.
v: A 30–45 minute devotional story stretched into a 3-hour TV-serial saga — until Prabhas arrives like a saviour for both the film AND the suffering audience 🙏😂
body:
For me, this is almost a 20-minute Prabhas film in which Manchu Vishnu does a lengthy 3-hour cameo 😂 Out of those three hours, he gives what may be his career-best performance for about three minutes — though even that is still mediocre-to-average when compared with many other Tollywood actors.

The film starts with an almost five-minute song giving us some background about the Srikalahasti temple. Around the interval, we get roughly ten minutes explaining the past relationship between Lord Shiva and Kannappa. And in the final few minutes we finally see what we had been waiting almost three hours for — why Kannappa is remembered as one of Lord Shiva’s greatest devotees.

This could have been a powerful 30–45 minute film with proper impact and screenplay. Unfortunately, the director chose to stretch it into a 3-hour-plus never-ending saga 🙏

In director Mukesh Kumar Singh’s defence, he came primarily from television serials rather than feature films — and he stayed very loyal to that experience by making this feel like an endlessly stretched TV saga, complete with mediocre television-level graphics.

When so much of the star cast and the cameos are reportedly working for little or no fee, and the producer still talks about a massive budget, audiences naturally expect grand visuals and strong CGI. Instead, we get blurred backgrounds and shots where you can almost feel the green screen. At times I wondered whether the team simply blurred things and hoped we would assume it was a censor issue 😂

For the first time, I found myself watching a Telugu movie while trying to read the subtitles just to understand the Telugu dialogues. Much of the dubbing sounds like international-school kids trying very carefully to pronounce Telugu with English accents — and in some cases you can hear Hindi, Tamil and Malayalam influences too 🙏

Mohan Babu, as usual, has proper command over the language and plays his part well. Sarathkumar tries hard to deliver clean Telugu, and you can actually hear the effort. Apart from him, I didn’t feel many actors — including Vishnu — worked enough on the diction.

The New Zealand locations also never gave me the native feel this story desperately needs. I kept thinking that forests in Kerala or North-East India may have given the film a far more rooted atmosphere 🤔

Between the accented Telugu, foreign-looking locations, heavy makeup and fake tattoos, I rarely got the feeling that I was watching a properly rooted Telugu devotional story ☹️

The first half is an absolute mess filled with cringe moments and dialogues. A few personal highlights:

  1. “Nemalini pelli chesukoni namili vadilestha!” 🙏😂
  2. The hero romances in front of his mother’s samadhi and then suddenly announces that there is no temple greater than that samadhi for him.
  3. The film has several women warriors, but many fight movements look as if dancers choreographed them instead of fight masters. Some sword moves feel more like dance poses than combat ☹️
  4. Several heroine shots could comfortably fit into old Liril soap advertisements 😂
  5. I still don’t understand the insistence on the old Raghavendra-Rao-school mixture of glamour and devotion. Even during devotional scenes, the styling gives me more glamour vibes than devotional emotion.

For the first time, I saw audiences in a PVR multiplex openly laughing, booing scenes and banging their heads during a movie that was supposed to be serious.

Then, sometime in the second half, Prabhas appears like a saviour — not only for the characters or for the film, but for the audience that has survived everything until then 🙏

Off late, I have complained about Prabhas’s lazy acting and dialogue-delivery style. Ironically, in this film the same style suddenly feels subtle and whistle-worthy. Maybe the role and dialogues suit him... or maybe my mind had already endured so much over-the-top acting from everyone else that normalcy itself felt extraordinary 😂

PS: My 12-year-old daughter forced me to add this line: “In the name of devotion, don’t take your kids to this movie and traumatise them.” 😭😂

e: Sekhar Kammula strips a familiar rich-vs-poor setup of hero worship and commercial formula, then lets Dhanush, Nagarjuna and the writing carry it. I enjoyed the realism, performances and philosophical dialogue, though the pacing may make it a harder recommendation for everyone.
v: A brave, near-realistic rich-vs-beggar drama with terrific performances — I enjoyed its offbeat approach even if I understand why the length may test some patience.
body:
There are a few kinds of movies where, while watching, you get sucked into a brilliant concept, near-realistic execution and career-best performances — yet you still walk out of the theatre feeling that something is missing.

KUBERAA is one such movie for me. I enjoyed the offbeat concept and narration, but I may still hesitate before recommending it blindly because I overheard quite a few audience members feeling that the film tested their patience.

Story-wise, we have seen plenty of Rich vs Poor movies with huge scope for pure commercial formula. What deserves appreciation is Sekhar Kammula’s decision to set up an Ultra Rich vs Beggar conflict in a near-realistic world with almost no conventional commercial elements 🙏

Especially the way he designs a few scenes — only a director who gives ZERO FUCKS about hero worship and commercial storytelling can pull off some of these choices 🙏

Acting-wise, Dhanush should be in serious contention for every award. His body language, smile, dialogue delivery — everything makes you believe that he has lived as a beggar for years. The only thing that put me off was that in a couple of scenes I felt Dhanush looked a little too healthy for the role 😂😉

In his vast career, I personally feel no role has suited Nagarjuna’s body language and voice modulation as perfectly as this one. It almost feels as if he was born to play this character 🫡

Initially, I was surprised why Sekhar chose Rashmika instead of someone like Sai Pallavi. After watching the film, I understood that this is probably one of the weaker female-character arcs in a Sekhar Kammula movie — and even then it is yards ahead of what heroines usually get in mainstream films.

Rashmika, despite her familiar “trying-to-be-cute” mannerisms, gives a much more mature performance here and fits the film better than I expected.

The only properly commercial element in the movie is DSP’s background music — and he uses it very well to elevate the intense scenes and deliver genuine goosebumps.

Special shout-out to the thought-provoking dialogues. The moment where Rashmika indirectly makes us realise that all of us are beggars in one way or another is pure philosophy 🙏

The length will definitely be a complaint for some people, but that’s true of almost every Sekhar Kammula film.

I also saw a few reviews complaining about the abrupt climax. Personally, I felt that with the film avoiding commercial shortcuts — the hero is neither educated enough to outsmart the corporate system nor powerful enough to beat everyone up — this is one of the only believable ways to reach the ending. Otherwise, it would have become a never-ending saga 🙄

e: BHAIRAVAM has a strong friendship-and-betrayal core, excellent BGM and cinematography, and committed performances from Nara Rohith, Manchu Manoj and Bellamkonda Sreenivas. Some Kantara-like echoes and an unresolved opening conflict hold it back, but it remains a very good effort for the team and budget.
v: A solid semi-rustic action drama and a welcome comeback vehicle for its three leads — very good for its scale, even if the remake baggage and missing closure stop it from being a must-watch.
body:
A semi-rustic rural action drama that could have become an impactful must-watch, but for me ends up as an overall Good Movie. Nevertheless, it is a much-needed comeback for Manchu Manoj, Nara Rohith and Bellamkonda Sreenivas.

STORY: The story is the heart and soul of this movie. The filmmakers waste no time and throw you directly into the plot from the beginning. The first five minutes may feel slightly suffocating because a lot of information is delivered through narration during the opening titles, but it prepares you for what follows.

The first half reminded me of Kantara in bits and pieces, but the multidimensional setup around friendship and betrayal is the real core of the film. I was so impressed with the story and had so many good things ready to say about Vijay Kanakamedala that I was genuinely disappointed when I later realised it was a REMAKE 🤐

DIRECTION: Since the story itself comes from the original film, there is less to discuss there. Vijay’s direction is good, but he should have taken basic care to avoid visual and plot similarities that immediately remind us of Kantara.

The other thing that bothered me was the lack of closure for the conflict established during the opening titles. One simple scene could have wrapped that thread up beautifully instead of leaving us to assume that the issue somehow got resolved 🤷

After back-to-back films with Allari Naresh in Naandhi and Ugram, Vijay now handles comeback roles for Nara Rohith, Manchu Manoj and Bellamkonda Sreenivas. At this rate, he may become the official Comeback Director for every actor waiting for a second innings 😊🥰

Sricharan Pakala’s BGM is too good, and the songs are catchy as well. The cinematography is top-notch and the visuals definitely create an impact.

Acting-wise, Nara Rohith is very much in his comfort zone. He has always had a habit of choosing niche subjects where the content does most of the talking and he can rely on his typical dialogue delivery and restrained expressions without unnecessary heroics 😉 He does exactly that here, carrying Vardha with subtlety.

Manchu Manoj, who has always been known for offbeat subjects, characters and acting styles, is back doing exactly what suits him. He is excellent in a grey-shaded role caught inside a moral conflict 🙏 This feels like a genuine comeback for him. If he can control that extra bit of over-expression and heavy dialogue delivery, I am sure he can do wonders in his second innings.

Kudos to Bellamkonda Sreenivas for attempting a character that almost behaves like a supporting role in the first half and then carries much of the second half. It is a complicated part that genuinely challenges his acting ability, and you can see the hard work 👍

Unfortunately, no matter how hard he works, some comparisons with what Rishab Shetty pulled off in Kantara become inevitable 😪 And I put the blame for that entirely on the director and the presentation, not on Bellamkonda.

Aditi Shankar stands out as the village girl and also with her dance moves. Her dubbing, however, needed more care because it never fully syncs with the rooted character. That was the main technical issue I noticed.

Overall, this is a Very Good Movie considering the team and budget.

PS: I genuinely don’t understand how the censor board works. How and why this movie received an A certificate is still a billion-dollar question for me 🫡

e: CREW works for me because it behaves like a straightforward commercial crime-comedy and lets its three leading ladies carry the fun. Logic takes a back seat at times, but the casting, witty writing and performances make that easy to forgive.
v: A proper women-led commercial entertainer with no need for agenda, propaganda or forced messaging — Tabu, Kareena and Kriti simply take over the screen 😍
body:
It’s been ages since Bollywood came up with a PROPER Women-Centric Movie without any agenda, propaganda or forced feminism. Kahaani is probably the last one that immediately comes to my mind — but while Kahaani was a crime thriller, CREW is a proper commercial entertainer 😍

And it boasts three wonderful artists in Tabu, Kareena Kapoor and Kriti Sanon.

Being a proper commercial movie, the content naturally has its own ups and downs when it comes to logic and cinematic freedom — the kind of things general Bollywood critics and so-called serious directors worry about a lot 😜 — but most of that goes for a toss once the performances take over.

Special kudos to the casting department for getting this combination so right!!!

All three — Tabu, Kareena and Kriti — are on fire, both in looks and performance, and carry the movie wonderfully on their shoulders 🙏

The part I enjoyed the most is the reversal of the usual hero-centric commercial movie. In those films, the heroines often have almost nothing to do. Here, in a proper women-centric commercial entertainer, the heroes have almost nothing to do 🤣

The special surprise is Kapil Sharma, who plays a wonderfully subtle role as Tabu’s husband — completely opposite to the loud energy we normally associate with him. He does a very good job 👍

If you have watched Rajesh Krishnan’s Lootcase, CREW has a similar comedy-crime flavour. This time, the story follows the ups and downs of three air hostesses, powered by witty dialogues and the chemistry and performances of its three leading ladies.

e: Tillu Square knows its audience already understands Tillu’s world, so it wisely avoids reinventing the formula. Siddhu remains the heart and soul, Anupama brings fresh energy and the returning characters make the sequel feel like another hilarious event in Tillu’s life.
v: A rare sequel that adds almost NOTHING new — and somehow that is exactly why it works. It simply gives Tillu fans what they came for, with an extra dose of Radhika kick 😍
body:
Even before stepping into the theatre for this sequel, you know exactly what kind of movie you are about to watch and you set your expectations accordingly. And that is probably Tillu Square’s biggest advantage!!!!

The biggest positive of DJ Tillu was the surprise element — the hero’s characterisation, costumes, one-liners and dialogue delivery all felt fresh.

In the second part, the biggest positive is completely different: the audience already knows what it is going to get.

Music, content and direction-wise, the team barely even tries to add anything dramatically new to the sequel — and surprisingly, that works 🙏

Apart from a few new major characters, almost everyone else continues from the original, making the story feel less like a giant “Part 2” and more like just another chaotic event in Tillu’s life!!!!

Siddhu is obviously the heart and soul of the film. Anupama brings a fresh dose of glamour and energy to the content... and the special appearance by the OG Radhika, Neha Shetty, gives the movie that extra kick 😍

Tillu Square is one of those rare sequels where nothing EXTRA is forced into the formula. It simply gives the audience exactly what they want — and still manages to make them laugh and enjoy it even more than the first part 🙏

e: GAAMI has an intriguing concept, ambitious interwoven screenplay and surprisingly strong camera/VFX work for its budget. The final twist keeps you guessing, but the painfully slow narration drains so much energy that the journey starts feeling eternal long before the climax arrives.
v: A genuinely unique concept with impressive visuals for its budget — unfortunately murdered by SLOOOOOOOOOOOW pacing from start to finish 😞
body:
A unique concept, narrated in a C/o Kancharapalem-style screenplay, with top-notch visuals for the limited budget and very good camera work — all of it SPOILED by SLOOOOOOOOOOOW-paced narration 😞

This is a perfect example of how one weak craft can pull down an otherwise interesting film.

Concept-wise, the team experiments with a genuinely unique storyline that grabs your attention and keeps you guessing about how everything may connect in the climax. The final twist can genuinely blow away your expectations.

That said, the twist may be difficult to digest for more conventional movie lovers. Audiences who enjoy unusual concepts may find it interesting — even if not completely convincing.

The screenplay is clearly reminiscent of C/o Kancharapalem. But in that film, the regular boy-next-door love stories make the audience emotionally connect with the different tracks. In GAAMI, the emotional and physical trauma of the characters can make the audience uncomfortable and slightly disconnected, which makes this kind of interwoven screenplay harder to absorb.

The BGM is apt for this world, and special mention must go to the cinematography and CGI teams for creating some genuinely impressive visual moments with the limited budget they had 🙏🙏

Acting-wise, it is refreshing to see Vishwak Sen in such a subtle and dull character after getting used to his highly energetic performances. He doesn’t have too many dramatic acting moments here — most of the role requires him to carry a sick, confused and emotionally distant expression throughout — and he stays within that tone.

The remaining cast also does a good job within the limitations of their characters.

Now coming to the main villain of the movie...

THE PAINFUL LAG!!!! 😞

Right from the word go until the climax, the pacing makes you feel as if you have been watching the film for an eternity. It slowly kills the excitement of wanting to discover how such a unique concept will unfold.

If you remember the Rubber Balaji character from Amrutham, at some point you may genuinely start wondering whether this movie was secretly directed by him 🤣

e: I went in expecting another Bollywood patriotic film built around familiar India-Pakistan beats and came out completely surprised. Hrithik and Deepika own the screen, but the spectacular aerial-action sequences are the real heart of FIGHTER and make this a proper big-screen 3D experience.
v: One of THE BEST Indian aerial-action experiences I have watched on the big screen — Hrithik, Deepika and those air-combat sequences absolutely demand 3D 🔥😍🫡
body:
Don’t miss this movie on the big screen with 3D glasses on!!!

To be frank, when the trailer dropped I wasn’t very excited. I assumed this would be just another Bollywood film cooking up a story around surgical strikes to cash in on patriotic sentiment...

But man, I was wrong!!!!

This is one of THE BEST INDIAN ACTION-WARFARE MOVIES I have watched on the big screen, and it absolutely deserves to be watched in 3D.

To start with... HRITHIK simply nails it with his Greek-God looks and amazing screen presence. And who better than Siddharth Anand to know how to project him on screen? He did it in Bang Bang!, did it again in WAR, and once again understands exactly how to use Hrithik’s charismatic personality in FIGHTER 😍

It was an absolute eye feast watching him in the Air Force uniform 🫡

DEEPIKA was 🔥 in this movie. In a few scenes she literally snatches your eyes away from Hrithik, which is no small achievement. She does a fantastic job, and the pairing of Hrithik & Deepika is total 😍

I genuinely wonder why it took Bollywood this long to cast them together 🙏

Content-wise, this is a tailor-made commercial patriotic film with the surgical-strike backdrop, good emotional beats, a little over-the-top patriotism and — obviously — Pakistan as the villain 😉

But beyond Hrithik and Deepika’s excellent screen presence, the ACTION is the heart and soul of this movie.

I had never seen aerial stunts of this scale in an Indian movie before. They genuinely give goosebumps and provide the WOW factor that separates FIGHTER from a regular patriotic action film.

Especially watch those sequences in 3D for a wonderful experience 🔥😍🫡

A MUST-WATCH for action-movie lovers and especially kids. And if you are a Hrithik or Deepika fan, then it is a proper Double Dhamaka for you guys!!!!!

e: HANU-MAN works because Prasanth Varma treats mythology, superhero cinema and mass-commercial ingredients as one package. The CGI is overhyped in places, but considering the budget the ambition is impressive, and the first and last ten minutes set up the larger universe extremely well.
v: Not a cult classic for me, but definitely a VERY GOOD superhero entertainer — smart mythology, solid mass elements and a BGM that does half the VFX team’s job 🔥🙏
body:
Let me make this clear: this is not a Cult Classic Movie for me, but it is definitely a VERY GOOD movie with a proper mix of science fiction, mythology and mass-commercial elements!!!

Prasanth Varma has always been a unique storyteller, and films like Awe, Kalki and Zombie Reddy are testimony to his story-writing ability. Here too, I liked the core idea — a guy who is obsessed with becoming a superhero eventually ending up as a supervillain. At least for me, that sounded fresh.

Direction-wise, Prasanth Varma does a very good job of mixing almost every commercial ingredient — mass moments, comedy, sentiment... everything except the mandatory special song 😜

The first and last ten minutes are the heart and soul of the movie. In the opening, he establishes the villain conflict extremely well. In the closing stretch, he sets the ground for the larger Prasanth Varma Cinematic Universe.

As the first film of a franchise, this is no less important than the first Iron Man movie was for the Avengers universe.

But barring those first and last ten minutes, much of the remaining movie is built using the regular bare-minimum commercial ingredients expected from a superhero film. That is why I still wouldn’t call this Prasanth Varma’s best work — especially after Awe made me go completely awestruck with his very first directorial effort!!!!!

Coming to the CGI, all the social-media posts going gaga over the “top-notch visuals” felt a little overhyped to me. There is definitely a lot of scope for improvement.

But considering the budget, the team has done very good work. Now that the film is successful, hopefully the upcoming films get bigger budgets and we genuinely get top-notch visuals.

Teja Sajja gives a very good performance and looks apt for the role. Vinay Rai is perfect as the stylish supervillain 🙂

The BGM is the soul of this movie. The music team does a fantastic job, especially with the Hanuman Chalisa-based portions.

Honestly, I feel a good portion of the appreciation currently going to the VFX team should also go to the music directors. That BGM takes the audience into a trance and dramatically enhances the visual impact of what is actually shown on screen.

Overall, content and taking-wise this is a good film. I also feel part of the cult-like appreciation comes from the fact that it was achieved with a relatively low budget and lesser-known star cast. The exact same output with a huge budget and famous stars may have received far more mixed reactions.

And of course, among Hindu gods, kids have a special affection for Lord Hanuman — and that emotional connection is a major backbone of the movie 🙏

e: Mahesh finally gives fans the massy, no-social-message commercial performance they have wanted for years, but Trivikram’s exhausted family-conflict writing gives him very little to work with. The star is energetic; the movie around him is disappointingly routine.
v: Definitely not another Agnyaathavaasi... but not a good film either. Mahesh Babu is the saving grace who somehow drags it into decent-watch territory 🙏
body:
Let me make this clear: this is not another Agnyaathavaasi... but it is not a good film either. Mahesh Babu is the major saving grace and somehow manages to make it a decent watch.

Mahesh finally tries to deliver what his fans have been asking from him for years — a proper commercial movie with NO SOCIAL MESSAGE 🙏

And he succeeds on his side with a terrific mass look, energetic dialogue delivery and an effort level we haven’t seen from him in a while. The only major mistake was trusting Trivikram to deliver the commercial film around him 😞

Kudos to Mahesh for genuinely giving his best at dancing too. Having a dancer like Sreeleela opposite you is a huge challenge to anyone’s dancing confidence 😂 But unlike some of his older attempts, this time he actually manages to pull it off instead of accidentally becoming the joke.

Trivikram seriously needs to stop cooking every commercial potboiler around family conflicts. There is hardly any juice left in that genre for him, and here he ends up filling the movie with unnecessary scenes simply to stretch the idea into a full-length film.

Yes, there are a couple of good dialogues here and there, but nothing that justifies the GURUJI tag or reminds me of his best writing 😞

It is high time he moves away from the family-conflict template and explores fresher concepts. And personally, I would also prefer him to focus completely on his own scripts rather than poking into PK’s scripts and creating confusion there as well as here 😜

Unlike Athadu and Khaleja — films that had underwhelming theatrical runs but eventually earned cult status — Mahesh and Trivikram seem to have desperately wanted their third collaboration to become an instant commercial success.

In trying to chase that immediate commercial formula, they seem to have forgotten what audiences actually expected from the Mahesh-Trivikram combination 🙄

Thaman probably needs a break too. None of the songs, for me, are up to the standards expected from a film starring a hero of this scale.

The BGM works reasonably well in the action episodes, but in a mother-child sentiment film it often sounded out of place — almost as if the score belonged to a thriller instead.

I also have a theory that Guruji originally hired Sreeleela for one dance number and then, for reasons known only to him, extended her dance performances into multiple scenes until she somehow became the main heroine 🙏😂

It is high time Sreeleela starts adding more acting to the Dancing, Dancing & Dancing — with occasional attempts to look cute in between.

Overall, I genuinely feel GUNTUR KAARAM with the same subject and treatment may have received slightly better reactions if it had been directed by someone other than Trivikram. The expectations attached to this combination simply expose how ordinary the film is.

e: Salaar feels like Prashanth Neel asking what would happen if Prabhas entered a KGF-sized world and then scaling the elevations, violence and action even further. The story beats may feel familiar, but the impact, Prabhas presentation and Prithviraj’s acting make the experience work.
v: Prashanth Neel takes the same elevation formula, turns every knob to 10X and uses Prabhas exactly the way his fans want — pure PAISA VASOOL if even 0.1% of you is a Prabhas fan 😍🙏
body:
An absolute eye feast for Prabhas fans... and after that ending, get ready for Salaar Part 2 🙏

Prashanth Neel was not joking when he described Salaar as his version of a Game of Thrones-style world — with Prabhas as the larger-than-life central warrior 😉

Prashanth Neel, take a bow. How many times can one director reuse the same basic formula of elevations, violence and action and still come out with flying colours? 🙏

Salaar feels like KGF multiplied several times in elevations, violence and stylish fights. For me, it is basically the answer to one question: what would happen if Prabhas had done KGF? 😍

Neel makes excellent use of Prabhas’s cut-out and, very smartly, gives him hardly any long dialogues. That itself is a masterstroke because in some recent films Prabhas’s dialogue delivery has been one of the weak points.

This may be one of the best uses of Prabhas’s screen presence. Man, Neel can create goosebumps using just the shadow of Prabhas — he doesn’t even need the full cut-out 🙇

There isn’t a huge acting burden on Prabhas here beyond delivering breathtaking poses, action moments and elevation shots. Prithviraj is the apt choice as Vardha and takes care of most of the conventional acting weight 🫡

Shruti Haasan has a relatively small role but does her job well. I particularly liked the way her NRI-English accent fit the character 👍

Ravi Basrur’s music may not be as extraordinary as his KGF work, but he does a very good job in the elevation and action episodes.

Special call-out to that engine-starting sound and the kids’ dialogues when Deva gets triggered 😍 Those small sound-design choices add so much to the buildup.

Content-wise, the first half strangely reminded me at times of Prabhas’s own Raghavendra, while the second half becomes a mixture of several familiar ideas.

Many individual scenes are not completely new and may give you a “seen this somewhere before” feeling — but the impact Neel creates still makes them worth watching.

1000% PAISA VASOOL if you are even a 0.1% Prabhas fan. For everyone else, imagine KGF-style filmmaking scaled up many times over 🙏

e: DUNKI has Hirani’s familiar mix of comedy and emotion, but the immigration struggle will naturally connect more strongly with NRIs and people who have faced visa problems. SRK is solid, Taapsee works well, but Vicky Kaushal gives the film its most powerful emotional stretch.
v: Not Rajkumar Hirani’s best, mainly because the core emotion is less universal — but still one of SRK’s strongest content-driven films of the last decade, with Vicky Kaushal stealing the emotional show 🥲
body:
The reason Rajkumar Hirani’s films — the Munna Bhai series, 3 Idiots, PK and others — became favourites of both critics and the public is simple: they usually have very universal content.

Mass audiences, class audiences, North Indians, South Indians, NRIs — almost everyone can connect to the core emotion, while Hirani mixes comedy and sentiment beautifully.

DUNKI still has a good mix of emotion and comedy, but what I felt was missing this time was that same universal connection to the central conflict.

NRIs, people who aspire to move abroad, or anyone who has personally dealt with visa problems will probably connect much more strongly with the plot. For others, it may be harder to fully understand why the characters feel so desperate about that journey.

Coming to SRK, after back-to-back massy characters he finally returns to a more content-driven role.

Somehow, though, I didn’t think he looked particularly convincing in the old-age portions — even though technically he was finally playing closer to his actual age 😉😂

I also think Bollywood should stop automatically adding heavy Punjabi nativity to every second emotional film. First, the Punjabi-influenced Hindi dialect can be difficult for audiences from other parts of India to fully follow. Second, not every leading actor naturally fits that cultural texture.

Even SRK didn’t completely suit the Punjabi flavour for me — though he was still far better than Aamir Khan in Laal Singh Chaddha 😜

Taapsee Pannu and the rest of the supporting cast portray their roles well.

And man... what a phase Vicky Kaushal is having 🙏 He is an absolute gem of an actor. His track is the real key to the movie’s emotional impact and contains the moments that can genuinely bring tears 🥲

Overall, this may not be Rajkumar Hirani’s best work, but even a weaker Hirani film is still better than the “best” work of plenty of other Bollywood directors 😄

Content-wise, it may connect deeply with a smaller section of the audience than his earlier films, but for SRK this is still one of the better content-driven roles he has had in the last decade.

e: ANIMAL is less a conventional movie and more an intentionally extreme experience: violent, vulgar, technically polished, frequently excessive and impossible to react to with a single emotion. Ranbir is phenomenal, the BGM and cinematography elevate the madness, and Sandeep Reddy Vanga goes far beyond anything he attempted in Arjun Reddy.
v: Probably the first FAMILY movie that you absolutely cannot watch with your family 😉 — a mad Vanga experience swinging from WOW to WTF, DELIGHT to DISGUST, and never playing safe.
body:
Sandeep Reddy Vanga is probably the first director in the history of world cinema to make a family movie that cannot be watched with family 😉

Rajamouli was absolutely right when he compared Sandeep Reddy Vanga to this generation’s Ram Gopal Varma. ANIMAL feels at least 10X of what Arjun Reddy was — in almost every possible way 🙏

If you are a traditional film lover, one of those intellectuals who immediately asks how a single person can bash hundreds of people, a viewer who cannot handle vulgar actions and dialogues on screen, or someone who expects every character to behave according to conventional morality... then this movie may simply not be for you. Please don’t waste your time 😄

This is not a movie that can be processed like a regular commercial film. For me, it is an EXPERIENCE where the WOW moments and the “what the fuck?” moments come in almost equal quantity.

In some portions you sympathise with the lead character; in others you hate him to the core. In a few scenes you admire how brilliantly something has been portrayed; in others you feel it has been dragged endlessly 🙏

All in all, it is a movie of wildly mixed emotions — taking you from DELIGHT to DISGUST, from WOW to YUCK!!!

Starting with the technical side, the title ANIMAL could not have been more appropriate. The BGM and cinematography are designed extremely well and constantly enhance the visual and audio experience of whatever madness is being unleashed on screen.

Acting-wise, I had very little doubt about who would dominate the awards conversation that season: Ranbir Kapoor. He completely owns this character.

Anil Kapoor does a terrific job as the father, and I was pleasantly surprised by both the characterisation and performance of Rashmika. If there is one genuinely sensible character inside this otherwise crazy world, it is Geetanjali — and Rashmika plays her very well 🙏

The rest of the cast also does its job effectively. Bobby Deol is almost a special appearance in a film running well over three hours, but even with limited screen time he creates a strong impact.

After Kabir Singh — the Hindi version of Arjun Reddy — Sandeep openly said in interviews that he was irritated by reviewers calling that movie “violent” and that one day he would show them what actual violence looks like.

Well... message received 😅

I am still in a trance wondering why and how he decided to use a family backdrop to unleash this level of mad violence. Whatever you think about the choices, the man is definitely a content creator with IRON BALLS 🙏

e: MANGALAVAARAM impressed me with both its courage and its craft. Ajay Bhupathi tackles physically and emotionally disturbing material without playing safe, Payal Rajput gives an exhausting committed performance, and the cinematography and Ajaneesh Loknath’s BGM turn the thriller into a haunting audiovisual experience.
v: I bow down to Ajay Bhupathi and his team 🙏 — BOLD, RAW, RUSTIC and technically stunning, with the guts to slap society’s hypocrisy right in the face.
body:
I bow down to the brilliance of Ajay Bhupathi and his team 🙏

I never expected such an out-and-out BOLD, RAW & RUSTIC Telugu movie — one that throws a direct slap in the face of a hypocritical society and delivers a simple but important message: instead of judging a book by its cover, maybe we should first understand what a person is going through physically and mentally.

It takes serious guts to write a story like this and execute it close to perfection.

And it takes equally serious guts for an actor to accept such a bold, emotionally exhausting role without worrying about where their career currently stands. Hats off to Payal Rajput for completely surrendering herself to the character 🫡

Dasaradhi Sivendra’s cinematography is top-notch. Honestly, a huge number of frames look wallpaper-worthy 😍 The low-light sequences in particular are beautifully shot and add enormously to the mood.

Music and BGM by Ajaneesh Loknath are the soul of this thriller. At its best, the score can give even Anirudh’s elevation BGM a run for its money.

And when I later realised that Ajaneesh was also the music director of Kantara, suddenly none of that quality surprised me 😍

Every character contributes effectively to the thriller atmosphere. Special shout-out to Ajay Ghosh — he was awesome 👍

Having praised all of that, I need to add one very clear warning.

This is a strict NO for sensitive viewers who cannot handle gut-wrenching emotions connected to sexual and physical abuse. The film does not make that material easy to watch.

If those subjects are personally difficult for you, it is genuinely better to skip this movie. Some of the visuals and emotions can stay with you and haunt you long after the film ends 😞

e: Tiger 3 finally gives Salman Khan a solid commercial film again. The story is wafer-thin and YRF’s Pakistan obsession is exhausting, but Salman-Katrina chemistry, entertaining action and the franchise’s continued respect for its female lead make it a decent spy entertainer.
v: Kabhi Eid... Kabhi Diwali... BHAI ke movie bina festival hai AADHURI 😉 A good Salman film after ages, even if Bollywood’s endless spy-universe overdose keeps it only a decent watch for me.
body:
Kabhi Eid... Kabhi Diwali...

BHAI ke movie bina festival hai AADHURI 😉😉

A good Salman Khan film after ages 🙏🙏🙏🙏 — which, for me, makes Tiger 3 a decent watch.

And when I say “decent”, part of that lukewarm reaction is simply because Bollywood has already overloaded us with so many spy thrillers.

When it comes to Bollywood spy films — and especially Yash Raj’s Spy Universe — I genuinely don’t understand the endless obsession with Pakistan.

Tiger 3 takes that obsession one level higher by having an Indian RAW agent effectively trying to protect democracy in Pakistan 🙏

On paper it sounds completely over-the-top, but then... anything is possible with Salman Bhai 😂 And surprisingly, at least while watching the film, I found myself accepting it.

I sincerely hope this is the last Spy Universe movie that revolves so heavily around Pakistan 🙏

One thing I have always liked about the Tiger franchise is that it was among the first fully commercial top-star franchises to give real importance to the female lead instead of using her as decoration.

Good to see that they continue doing that here. Katrina’s Zoya still matters to the story and the action.

Like almost every other spy movie, the core storyline is wafer-thin and has plenty of flaws. But the action sequences and the chemistry between the actors compensate enough to make it a good watch — even if I wouldn’t call it a must-watch.

For people comparing the craze of Tiger 3 with Pathaan, I would remind them that a huge part of Pathaan’s excitement came from SRK doing a full-fledged spy-action film for the first time.

I genuinely wonder whether a Pathaan sequel — if and when it comes — can recreate the same frenzy.

Salman, meanwhile, is doing this effortlessly even in the third Tiger instalment. That shows the command he still has over the masses.

All he really needs to do is bend his back a little and select better scripts... but a serious NO TO TUBELIGHT please 😉😂

The one proper disappointment for me is the music. Forget comparing it with Pathaan — even the first two Tiger films had much peppier and more memorable songs.

The songs here? 😏

e: SKANDA lost me from the very first scene and never found a way back. A hero introduced as a foreign-university topper and ethical hacker solves everything by flexing muscles, the action becomes parody-level excess, and Thaman’s usually helpful BGM only amplifies the chaos.
v: Nolan gaadi movies decode cheyatam kaadhu raaa... meeku dammunte maa Boyaaa anna SKANDA decode cheyandi 🙏🤣 Ram’s looks and the dances survive; almost everything else is unbearable.
body:
Nolan gaadi movies decode cheyatam kaadhu raaa... meeku dammunte maa Boyaaa anna SKANDA decode cheyandi 🙏🙏🙏🤣

This is what happens when filmmakers start assuming their audience has absolutely no sense.

I completely agree that plenty of illogical mass-masala films have become blockbusters. But the successful ones usually grab your attention through at least one department — comedy, emotion, heroism, music, action, something — strongly enough that you voluntarily forget the logic and enjoy what is being shown.

Unfortunately, SKANDA disconnected me right from the first scene itself. After that, I never found a reason to reconnect either with the movie or with its plot.

When you establish your hero as a foreign-university topper and an outstanding ethical hacker, the bare minimum expectation is that at some point he may use his INTELLIGENCE to corner the villains — who, in this case, happen to include the Chief Ministers of two states 🤣😉

But... BUT... BUT...

That would apparently be Nolan’s way of filmmaking.

In Boya’s universe, the hero simply flexes his muscles and solves everything with physical power. That’s it 🙏

Some of the action sequences looked as if they were choreographed by Mutton Kottu Masthan 🤣

Normally, Thaman has this wonderful ability to take an ordinary scene and lift it to the next level with his BGM.

Ironically, that becomes a huge minus here. The scenes are already so ridiculously over-the-top that adding Thaman’s high-energy score pushes them from excessive to almost unbearable 🫡

Taking-wise, the movie is shot in classic Boyapati style: the screen is packed with hundreds of character artists whose primary job is to dress loudly, make exaggerated expressions and deliver over-the-top dialogues praising either the hero or the villain 🙏

For me, the only real positives are Ram’s looks and the Ram-Sreeleela dance combinations.

Except for those two things... almost everything else was unbearable.

e: Miss Shetty Mr Polishetty impressed me with how comfortably it handles a bold modern relationship idea without making the audience uncomfortable. Naveen proves he is far more than a comedy actor, Anushka fits the mature character beautifully, and the writing balances witty one-liners with genuine emotion.
v: A beautiful, bold and mature new-age love story — Mahesh Babu balances a potentially uncomfortable subject with comedy, emotion and grace almost effortlessly 🙏😍
body:
An excellent movie for the new-age audience...

First and foremost, I need to talk about the brilliance of writer-director Mahesh Babu P. He takes a genuinely bold subject, blends it with subtle comedy and presents it in a way that can appeal to a much larger audience without constantly making them feel awkward.

The witty one-liners and the emotional dialogues are very nicely balanced 🙏

This may have been his debut as a director, but the ease with which he handles a mature love story reminded me of filmmakers like Karan Johar and Imtiaz Ali when they are at their best in the relationship space 😍

Naveen Polishetty is a true actor. His ability is definitely not limited to comedy. Man, he is equally effective in the emotional scenes here.

More than anything else, it is Naveen’s performance that makes the chemistry between Anushka and him feel so adorable and believable despite the unusual setup 🙏

Anushka’s screen presence has naturally changed over the years, but acting-wise she is absolutely on point and suits the mature-woman character perfectly.

Kudos to the production house and the director for having the courage to bring together an established star heroine and an upcoming-but-highly-talented actor for a bold story — and then present that story so beautifully and gracefully 🙏🙏🙏

Special mention again to the dialogues, whether comedy or emotional. They do a lot of the heavy lifting without sounding like forced “message” writing 🫡

The only disappointment I had was with the stand-up-comedy portions. They could have been much sharper and more engaging. Ironically, I found some of the regular conversational scenes funnier than the actual stand-up material 😞

Nevertheless, I walked out of the theatre with the satisfaction of having watched a beautiful, bold and mature love story.

e: JAWAN offers very little that feels new to a regular South Indian commercial-cinema audience, but that barely matters when Atlee packages familiar social-message and mass ingredients around SRK with this much energy. Nayanthara and Vijay Sethupathi are strong, but SRK steals the show because... BAAP baap hota hai 😉
v: If Pathaan was the starter for SRK fans, JAWAN is the full SOUTH INDIAN MASS THALI 😍🤣 — familiar ingredients for us, but watching SRK go full Rajini-style commercial is pure fan treat.
body:
If Pathaan was just the starter for an SRK fan, JAWAN is the proper full-fledged, yummy-in-your-tummy SOUTH INDIAN MASS TREAT 😍🙏🙏🙏

All of a sudden, SRK seems to have decided to become Rajini for one movie — and for his fans, it is a pure massy celebration.

Vijay Sethupathi and Nayanthara both shine and do an excellent job, but by the end it is SRK who steals the show... kyon ki woh BAAP hai 😉

The BGM is good, but for me it still doesn’t reach the crazy standards Anirudh himself has set with some of his previous work 😢

Special mention to the one-line dialogues. They are designed exactly to give fans that instant theatrical kick 🙏🙏

Content-wise, I have a funny theory: during lockdown, SRK probably watched a marathon of South Indian commercial movies and decided he wanted one single film containing all their favourite social-message ingredients 😂

  1. Bank frauds and loan-system issues — Sarkaru Vaari Paata vibes.
  2. The poor condition of government healthcare — shades of films like Ganesh.
  3. The importance of voting for the right candidates — Sarkar territory.
  4. Cute father-daughter sentiment — Theri flavour.
  5. A massy father-son commercial setup — Bigil-style energy.
  6. And of course, a hero surrounded by a powerful gang of women — again very much in Atlee’s comfort zone.

So SRK calls Atlee — the director of Theri and Bigil — and Atlee creates one giant commercial khichdi, taking familiar ingredients from all over South Indian cinema, applying his trademark screenplay and direction... and BANG, one of SRK’s best pure commercial entertainers is ready 😍🤣

For a regular South Indian moviegoer, the film offers almost nothing genuinely new in terms of ideas.

But there is still one very big novelty: watching SRK surrender himself completely to an out-and-out South-style commercial movie.

And one thing is for sure — JAWAN will definitely open more doors for top South Indian directors to work with the biggest Bollywood stars.

e: KUSHI is pleasant more than powerful. Vijay Deverakonda is back in a likeable boy-next-door zone, Samantha fits the grounded role easily and their chemistry carries the film, but the interesting atheist-vs-believer marriage conflict never reaches the emotional depth its premise promises.
v: A good, decent entertainer that gives neither a major HIGH nor a major disappointment — Vijay and Samantha’s fresh chemistry makes it an easy one-time watch.
body:
A good, decent entertainer that neither gives you any major HIGH nor disappoints you badly either...

After the LIGER debacle, Vijay Deverakonda is back to playing a boy-next-door kind of character — and he is genuinely enjoyable in this space.

After watching him here, I strongly feel he should try one proper out-and-out comedy role at least once. I am pretty sure he would kill it with ease!!!

After a long gap, Samantha also gets a role that doesn’t depend on her stardom to carry it. It is a relatively normal girl-next-door character, and she slips into it comfortably.

More than the individual acting power of the lead pair, it is their fresh pairing and cute chemistry that works best for the film.

The first half is decent and easily passable, mainly setting up the characters and allowing the chemistry to develop. The real conflict arrives in the second half.

On paper, the idea of problems inside a new marriage — with an atheist on one side and an orthodox believer on the other — sounds genuinely interesting.

But the execution never becomes as effective as the concept deserves, especially when the setup naturally invites comparison with old Mani Ratnam classics that handled newlywed-couple conflicts with much more emotional depth.

It is also slightly disappointing considering Shiva Nirvana’s own standards. His first two movies were excellent, if not outright classics, so I expected this emotional conflict to land much harder.

I personally felt the climax had a strong point to convey but was not executed properly 😞

Overall, though, KUSHI remains a good one-time watch. You may not remember it forever, but you probably won’t regret watching it on the big screen either!!!!

e: OMG 2 connected with me almost scene by scene. The way it blends sex education, religion, humour and courtroom drama makes a difficult subject accessible without diluting its message, while Pankaj Tripathi, Yami Gautam, Akshay Kumar and the supporting cast elevate already strong writing.
v: Some movies entertain, some enlighten — OMG 2 does BOTH while tackling a taboo subject with courage, humour and intelligence. A MUST-WATCH for parents 🙏🙏🙏
body:
You watch some movies for entertainment and some for enlightenment...

Very rarely do you find a movie that manages to ENTERTAIN & ENLIGHTEN you about subjects society still treats as taboo.

Fortunately, OMG 2 falls exactly into that rare category 🙏🙏🙏

The way the creators blend sexual education with religion is terrific and hard-hitting. More importantly, that combination helps the core message connect with the masses instead of becoming a dry classroom lecture.

For me, this is a MUST-WATCH for parents who genuinely want to understand some of the issues and confusion their teenage children may go through.

I connected so strongly with the movie that almost every major scene and dialogue felt clap-worthy.

The strong content is elevated even further by excellent actors like Pankaj Tripathi, Yami Gautam and Akshay Kumar, along with the supporting cast. Almost everyone gives 200% justice to their respective roles!!!

When I watched the first OMG, I was extremely impressed with the concept and writing.

But honestly, for me, OMG 1 is nothing when compared with the brilliance of OMG 2.

You may or may not personally like the film depending on your sensibilities and how open you are to discussing the taboo around sexual education.

But irrespective of that discomfort, if you are a parent, I genuinely believe this is a movie you should watch.

e: I entered GADAR 2 worried that my changed sensibilities might ruin the affection I still had for the 2001 original. Within 15 minutes, the nostalgia took over. Once Tara Singh enters Pakistan, logic disappears, the goosebumps return and Sunny Deol reminds you exactly why this character became iconic.
v: Twenty-two years later, Tara Singh made me forget logic, changed sensibilities and all my grown-up perspectives — pure nostalgia, goosebumps and Sunny Deol mass magic 🙏😇
body:
Back in 2001, I had just stepped into Intermediate First Year. This was much, much before the social-media era, and there was unusual euphoria in Guntur around a couple of newly released Hindi films — at a time when even getting a direct Hindi release in town was relatively rare.

As a teenager with limited understanding of the world and still building my own perspectives, I absolutely loved the innocence of Tara Singh and the love story between him and his Madam Ji!!!!

Then came the second half... and I got full goosebumps watching Tara Singh bash Pakistani goons and army men with his bare hands — with a little assistance from that iconic hand pump 😇

Cut to 22 years later.

When GADAR 2 was announced, I was genuinely sceptical about how I would react to it. My sensibilities had changed, my perspective on borders and people had changed, and I was worried that the sequel might now look cringe to me — or worse, somehow damage the affection I still had for GADAR.

So I stepped into the theatre with all those doubts and with a fairly good idea of what the story would be.

BUT... BUT... BUT...

Within 10–15 minutes, I forgot almost all my perspectives, sensibilities and logic and got completely sucked into the movie 😂

I actually became restless waiting for Tara Singh to enter Pakistan. And once he does... the familiar goosebumps return.

I thoroughly enjoyed the way the director plays with nostalgia, bringing back glimpses and memories from the first GADAR at exactly the moments designed to trigger old fans.

And YES — the iconic hand pump makes a comeback too... but this time with dignity 🤣

More than anything, GADAR 2 feels like a tribute to Sunny Deol.
